requirements.title: Provider-specific template implementation
requirements.description: The user can choose a commerce provider from a list of supported providers (e.g., Shopify, BigCommerce, Ecwid, etc.). Each provider has its own repository and demo link, allowing the user to fork the main repository and replace the `lib/shopify` file with their own implementation while keeping the rest of the template mostly unchanged.
requirements.userAction: The user selects a commerce provider from the provided list.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The user is directed to the corresponding provider's repository and demo, and can fork the main repository to swap out the provider-specific implementation.

requirements.title: Provider demo availability
requirements.description: Each listed provider has a demo link that the user can visit to see a live example of the commerce template running with that provider. This helps the user evaluate the provider's integration before implementing it.
requirements.userAction: The user clicks on a provider's demo link.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The user is taken to a live demo site that showcases the commerce template with that provider's backend.

requirements.title: Asset download for providers
requirements.description: Providers can download a set of assets (e.g., images, icons) from a shared Google Drive link to use in their own demo implementations. This ensures consistency across provider demos.
requirements.userAction: The user (provider) clicks on the asset download link.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The user is taken to a Google Drive folder where they can download the assets for their demo.

requirements.title: Install Orama Search Integration
requirements.description: Users can integrate Orama into Next.js Commerce to upgrade search functionality. This adds typeahead with dynamic re-rendering, vector-based similarity search, and JavaScript-based configuration. For smaller catalogs, search runs entirely in the browser; for larger ones, it runs on a CDN.
requirements.userAction: Install and configure the Orama search integration in Next.js Commerce.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The product's search is upgraded with typeahead, dynamic re-rendering, and vector-based similarity search, with search operations running in the browser or on a CDN based on catalog size.

requirements.title: Install React Bricks Visual CMS Integration
requirements.description: Users can integrate React Bricks into Next.js Commerce to visually edit pages, product details, and footer content. This provides a visual headless CMS that allows editing content directly on the site.
requirements.userAction: Install and configure the React Bricks visual headless CMS integration in Next.js Commerce.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The product allows visual editing of pages, product details, and footer content through a CMS interface.

requirements.title: Set up environment variables
requirements.description: The user must configure environment variables to run the application. They can either use Vercel Environment Variables or create a local .env file with the values from .env.example.
requirements.userAction: The user sets up environment variables using Vercel or a .env file.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The application has the necessary configuration to connect to Shopify and other services.

requirements.title: Install Vercel CLI and link local instance
requirements.description: The user installs the Vercel CLI globally and links their local project to their Vercel and GitHub accounts. This creates a .vercel directory and allows downloading environment variables.
requirements.userAction: The user runs 'npm i -g vercel' and then 'vercel link' in the project directory.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The local project is linked to Vercel and GitHub, and a .vercel directory is created.

requirements.title: Download environment variables
requirements.description: After linking, the user downloads the environment variables from Vercel to their local machine using the Vercel CLI.
requirements.userAction: The user runs 'vercel env pull' in the project directory.
requirements.expectedOutcome: Environment variables are downloaded and available for the application.

requirements.title: Install dependencies and start development server
requirements.description: The user installs project dependencies with pnpm and starts the development server. The application should then be accessible at localhost:3000.
requirements.userAction: The user runs 'pnpm install' followed by 'pnpm dev'.
requirements.expectedOutcome: The application runs locally and is accessible at http://localhost:3000/.
